ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a rectangle labeled 30 cm across the bottom. Its height is split by a middle horizontal line into two equal parts, each labeled 14 cm on the left. Inside the rectangle are four shaded congruent triangles arranged around the central region. Two shaded triangles have vertical sides spanning a 14 cm half-height, and the corresponding sides of the left and right shaded triangles lie along the middle horizontal line. Reasoning: Since the four triangles are identical, those corresponding horizontal middle-line segments each measure 14 cm. The total rectangle width is 30 cm, so the small horizontal gap between the two interior vertical sides is 30 - 14 - 14 = 2 cm. Each triangle can be treated as having base 14 cm and perpendicular height 2 cm. Thus the area of one triangle is (1/2) * 14 * 2 = 14 cm^2. With 4 identical triangles, the total area is 4 * 14 = 56 cm^2.

raw_record.question_text: The picture shows a rectangle with four identical triangles. Determine the total area of the triangles.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the outer rectangle is 30 cm wide and is split horizontally into two 14 cm-high halves. The four shaded triangles are stated to be identical. In the drawing, two of the triangles have a vertical side spanning one 14 cm half-height of the rectangle, and the corresponding sides of the left and right triangles lie along the middle horizontal line. Therefore the left horizontal segment and the right horizontal segment corresponding to those 14 cm sides each measure 14 cm. Subtract these from the total 30 cm width to get the small horizontal gap between the two interior vertical sides: 30 - 14 - 14 = 2 cm. Each identical triangle can then be viewed with base 14 cm and perpendicular height 2 cm, so one triangle has area 1/2 * 14 * 2 = 14 cm^2. Multiply by 4 identical triangles to get the total area 56 cm^2.
